བརྟེན་ཏེ་གང་ཡིན་པ། །དེ་ནི་དེ་ལས་གཞན་མི་འཐད། །འདི་ལ་ཁྱོད་གཞན་ཞེས་བྱ་བར་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ནི་དེ་ལས་གཞན་པ་འགའ་ཞིག་ལ་#བརྟེན་ཏེ་གཞན་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་ཡིན་ན། གཞན་མེད་ན་གཞན་ནི་རང་ལས་གཞན་དུ་མི་འགྱུར་རོ། །ཡང་གཞན་
ཡང་། གང་ལ་བརྟེན་ཏེ་གང་འབྱུང་བ་དེ་ནི་དེ་ལས་གཞན་ཡིན་པར་མི་འཐད་དོ། །འདིར་སྨྲས་པ། གལ་ཏེ་གཞན་ཡིན་པར་འགྱུར་#ན་དེས་སྐྱོན་ཅི་ཞིག་ཏུ་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར། འདིར་བཤད་པ། གལ་ཏེ་གཞན་ནི་གཞན་ལས་གཞན། །གཞན་མེད་པར་ཡང་རུང་བར་འགྱུར། །གཞན་ལས་
གཞན་པའི་གཞན་པ་དེ། །མེད་ན་མེད་པས་དེའི་#ཕྱིར་མེད། །གལ་ཏེ་གང་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་གཞན་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་དེ། དེ་ལས་གཞན་ཡིན་པར་གྱུར་ན་ནི། གཞན་དེ་མེད་པར་ཡང་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་རུང་བར་འགྱུར་བས་དེ་ནི་མི་འཐད་དོ། །ཅི་#སྟེ་འདི་སྙམ་དུ་གཞན་ནི་གཞན་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་གཞན་དུ་
འགྱུར་བར་སེམས་ན། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་གཞན་གང་ལས་གཞན་པའི་གཞན་པ་དེ་#མེད་ན་གཞན་མེད་པས་རང་ཉིད་ལས་གཞན་ཉིད་དུ་མི་འགྱུར་བ་དེའི་ཕྱིར་གཞན་མེད་པ་#ཁོ་ནར་ཤེས་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག །འདིར་སྨྲས་པ། རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་པར་འབྱུང་བ་ནི་གཞན་ཉིད་མ་ཡིན་མོད་ཀྱི་འོན་ཀྱང་གཞན་ཉིད་
ཅེས་བྱ་བ་སྤྱི་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ལ་ལྟོས་ནས་དེ་གཞན་ཉིད་དུ་འགྱུར་རོ། །འདིར་བཤད་པ། གཞན་ཉིད་གཞན་ལ་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །གཞན་མ་ཡིན་ལའང་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན#། །གཞན་ཉིད་ཡོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ན། །གཞན་ནམ་དེ་ཉིད་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །ཁྱོད་ཀྱིས་གཞན་ཉིད་ཅེས་བྱ་བ་སྤྱི་གང་ཡིན་
པ་དེ་ལ་ལྟོས་ནས་དེ་གཞན་དུ་འགྱུར་རོ་ཞེས་སྨྲས་པ་དེས་ན། དེ་ལྟ་ན་རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་པར་འབྱུང་བ་ཉིད་དུ་སྨྲས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནམ། གཞན་ཡང་གཞན་ཉིད་ཅེས་བྱ་བ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ཡང་དངོས་པོ་ལ་བརྟེན་ཅིང་ལྟོས་#ནས་འགྲུབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་ནི་དངོས་པོ་ལས་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་ཡོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ལ། 
གཞན་མ་ཡིན་པ་ལ་ཡང་ཡོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ།# །གཞན་ཉིད་ཡོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ན་གཞན་ནམ་གཞན་མ་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ཉིད་དུ་རྣམ་པར་བརྟགས་#པ་དེ་གཉི་ག་ཡང་ཡོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ཡང་གཞན་ཡང་། དེ་ནི་དེ་དང་ཕྲད་པ་མེད། །གཞན་དང་གཞན་ཡང་ཕྲད་མི་འགྱུར། །ཕྲད་བཞིན་པ་དང་ཕྲད་པ་

in dependence on something
Is illogical as being other than that.

That which you fixate upon as "other" becomes "other" only in dependence on some other thing; without that other, it would not be other than itself. Furthermore, that which arises in dependence on something is illogical as being other than it. To this, it is said: "If it were other, what fault would follow?" To this, it is explained:

If the other were other than the other,
It would be so even without the other.
But since that otherness from another
Does not exist, it does not exist.

If that which becomes "other" in dependence on something were indeed other than it, then it would be appropriate for it to be other even without that thing; but that is illogical. If you think that the other is other in dependence on another, then since the otherness from another does not exist, the "other" itself does not exist; therefore, know that there is no otherness. To this, it is said: "Dependent origination is indeed not otherness, but it becomes other in relation to the general category of 'otherness'." To this, it is explained:

Otherness does not exist in the other,
Nor does it exist in the non-other.
If otherness does not exist,
Neither the other nor that very thing exists.

When you say it becomes "other" in relation to the general category of "otherness," are you not simply describing dependent origination? Furthermore, since "otherness" itself is established in dependence and relation to things, it does not exist apart from things, nor does it exist in what is not other. If otherness does not exist, then neither the "other" nor "that very thing" <note>the self-same</note> exist as separate analytical categories. Furthermore:

That very thing does not meet with itself,
Nor does the other meet with the other.
The meeting, the met,
head: That which exists
tail: And the meeter do not exist.
old_translation:
It is said here: If it were "other," what fault would follow?

To this, it is explained:
If another were "other" than another,
It would be possible even without that another.
But since that otherness from which another is "other"
Is absent, it does not exist.
If that which becomes "other" by depending on something else were actually "other" than it, then it should be possible for it to be so even without that other; but that is not logical. If you think that another becomes "other" by depending on another, then since there is no "otherness" without the other from which it is "other," understand that otherness itself does not exist.

It is said here: Although dependent origination is not "otherness," nevertheless, in relation to the general category of "otherness," it becomes "other."

To this, it is explained:
Otherness is not in another,
Nor is it in the non-other.
If otherness does not exist,
Neither the other nor the same exists.
Since you said that something becomes "other" by relating to the general category of "otherness," have you not then spoken of dependent origination itself? Furthermore, since that which is called "otherness" is established by depending on and relating to entities, it does not exist apart from entities, nor does it exist in what is not "other." If otherness does not exist, then neither of the two analyzed states — the "other" or the "same" <note>literally: "that itself"</note> — exists.

Furthermore:
That does not meet with itself,
Nor does another meet with another.
The process of meeting, the met,
And the meeter do not exist.
The same thing does not meet with itself. Why? Because it is one; the same cannot meet with the same. Another does not meet with another either. Why? Because they are distinct; distinct things are not desired to meet, and there is no purpose for it. Thus, when one logically analyzes and finds that contact is not established in entities, the process of meeting, the met, and the meeter also do not exist, just like heaven and earth <note>never touching</note>.

This is called the Examination of Contact, the fourteenth chapter.

<summary>This page concludes the analysis of contact by refuting the existence of "otherness" and "sameness." It argues that since things cannot meet themselves or each other, the entire concept of contact is empty.</summary>
<keywords>otherness, sameness, dependent origination, contact, meeting, meeter, Examination of Contact</keywords>
